candidate_changes.adaptive_mixed: Adaptive retained with paired evidence. Mixed dropped as a default assignment.

archetypes.name: Precision and stability orientation
archetypes.operational_definition: Consistent corner-relative input and line under repeated matched tasks. Pace and preferred balance are independent attributes.
archetypes.limitations: Piastri cited prior junior-category feedback. This is a hypothesis for feature design, with no numerical F1 fingerprint.
archetypes.misleading_cases: Device filtering and a stable setup can produce similar traces.

archetypes.name: Entry rotation
archetypes.operational_definition: Greater share of total heading change before the fixed apex, supported by yaw, path and input context.
archetypes.limitations: Senna and Alonso provide distinct, context-bound examples of yaw or trajectory strategies. Public yaw is unavailable at the required fidelity.
archetypes.misleading_cases: A responsive front preference, transient oversteer or a sharp turn-in can occur independently.

archetypes.name: Brake and turn overlap
archetypes.operational_definition: Continuous spectrum from early brake release before turn-in to sustained overlap with declining command. Estimate in a fixed entry window.
archetypes.limitations: The McLaren comparison motivates a relative axis under the MCL39 context. The two reports share a source.
archetypes.misleading_cases: Heavy stops and linked bends demand different overlaps. Binary brake cannot reveal command release shape.

archetypes.name: Minimum-speed retention
archetypes.operational_definition: Higher minimum speed relative to matched approach in a fixed corner window, evaluated with downstream time and exit acceleration.
archetypes.limitations: Working measurement hypothesis. No general driver assignment.
archetypes.misleading_cases: Vehicle grip and exit compromise can dominate. Minimum speed need not coincide with geometric apex.

archetypes.name: Entry and exit emphasis
archetypes.operational_definition: Jointly characterize time and speed over entry, apex, exit and next straight. Record entry and exit evidence independently.
archetypes.limitations: Massa and Ocon described individual sequences where preparation for the following turn or straight affects line choice.
archetypes.misleading_cases: A local time gain may reverse by the next braking zone. Energy deployment changes straight time.

archetypes.name: Traction modulation
archetypes.operational_definition: Sustained throttle rise, corrective commands and simulated driven-axle slip within the same exit demand.
archetypes.limitations: One wet start and line analysis provides context, with no public numerical pedal or tyre-slip reference.
archetypes.misleading_cases: Traction control, wet conditions, ERS and controller maps can change apparent smoothness.

archetypes.name: Context-dependent adaptation
archetypes.operational_definition: Repeatable feature shifts across paired setup, grip or task conditions with adequate overlapping samples.
archetypes.limitations: Context and testimony can guide the matched conditions. Magnitude is undefined without controlled repeated observations.
archetypes.misleading_cases: Sparse coverage cannot establish a mixed style. Team swaps bundle multiple causes.

archetypes.name: High-speed commitment
archetypes.operational_definition: Relative speed retention and lift behaviour in a specific high-speed class at the same aero mode and grip.
archetypes.limitations: Sources motivate circuit-conditional hypotheses about instability and long fast corners.
archetypes.misleading_cases: Full throttle can be vehicle- or deployment-limited. Public throttle semantics need calibration.
